test_title: RRB Group D Official Paper (Held On: 11 Dec, 2025 Shift 2)
subject: general
question: Two banks, A and B, offered loans at 3.5% and 7.5% per annum, respectively. Mukund borrowed an amount of ₹2,00,000 from each bank. Find the positive difference (in ₹) between the amounts of simple interest paid to the two banks by Mukund after 2 years.
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Rate difference per year = 7.5% − 3.5% = 4%.

Interest difference for 1 year = 4% of 2,00,000 = 8,000.

Interest difference for 2 years = 8,000 × 2 = 16,000.

**∴ The correct option is A.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Principal (P) = ₹2,00,000

Rate 1 (R₁) = 3.5% p.a. | Rate 2 (R₂) = 7.5% p.a.

Time (T) = 2 years

**Formula Used:**

Simple Interest (SI) = (P × R × T) ÷ 100

 Principal ₹2,00,000 
• 
• Bank A (3.5%) SI = ₹14,000 Bank B (7.5%) SI = ₹30,000 
 Difference: ₹16,000 

**Calculations:**

⇒ SI paid to Bank A = (2,00,000 × 3.5 × 2) ÷ 100

⇒ SI paid to Bank A = 2,000 × 7 = ₹14,000

⇒ SI paid to Bank B = (2,00,000 × 7.5 × 2) ÷ 100

⇒ SI paid to Bank B = 2,000 × 15 = ₹30,000

⇒ Difference = ₹30,000 − ₹14,000

⇒ Difference = ₹16,000

**∴ The correct option is A.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Difference in Simple Interest

When the principal and time are the same, the difference in SI for two different rates R₁ and R₂ is given by P × T × (R₁ − R₂) ÷ 100.

Effective Interest Rate

The effective interest rate for a period is R × T%. For example, 3.5% for 2 years results in a total interest of 7% of the principal.

Total Amount in SI

Amount (A) = P + SI = P × [1 + (R × T) ÷ 100].
